title: User directory
context: Trust & Safety wants a clean directory of everyone on the platform.
task: List every user's name, country and age, ordered alphabetically by name.
hint: No filter needed — just pick the three columns and decide how to sort the full list.
answer: SELECT name, country, age FROM users ORDER BY name, user_id;

title: Creators
context: Accounts flagged as creators unlock monetisation tools.
task: Return the user_id and name of every user who is a creator.
hint: Creator status is stored as a flag on the users table — keep only the ones switched on.
answer: SELECT user_id, name FROM users WHERE is_creator = 1;

title: Instagram reels
context: The growth team tracks reels as its priority format.
task: Return post_id, user_id and reach for every reel published on Instagram.
hint: Two conditions must both hold — one on the app, one on the format.
answer: SELECT post_id, user_id, reach FROM posts WHERE platform = 'Instagram' AND post_type = 'reel';

title: High-reach posts
context: The insights team is studying posts that travelled widely.
task: Return post_id and reach for posts seen by more than 3,000 people.
hint: Filter on how many people the post reached.
answer: SELECT post_id, reach FROM posts WHERE reach > 3000;

title: Young adults
context: An ad set targets a few specific younger ages.
task: Return name and age for users who are exactly 18, 22 or 24.
hint: Age has to match one of a small set of values.
answer: SELECT name, age FROM users WHERE age IN (18, 22, 24);

title: Core ad segment
context: The 25-to-34 bracket is the core advertising segment.
task: Return user_id and age for users aged 25 to 34 inclusive.
hint: An inclusive range on age.
answer: SELECT user_id, age FROM users WHERE age BETWEEN 25 AND 34;

title: Beyond the like
context: The reactions team studies engagement richer than a plain like.
task: Return reaction_id, post_id and reaction for every reaction that is something other than a like.
hint: You want the rows that do not match one value.
answer: SELECT reaction_id, post_id, reaction FROM reactions WHERE reaction <> 'like';

title: Platforms in use
context: A report needs the list of apps that people actually post to.
task: Return each platform that appears in the posts table, with no duplicates.
hint: A platform shows up on many posts — you want each one listed only once.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT platform FROM posts;

title: Names starting with A
context: Support is working an alphabetical batch of accounts.
task: Return name for users whose name starts with the letter A.
hint: Pattern-match the start of the text.
answer: SELECT name FROM users WHERE name LIKE 'A%';

title: Most-liked posts
context: The editorial team features the best-performing posts.
task: Return post_id, user_id and likes for the five posts with the most likes.
hint: Sort by likes, most first, then keep only the top few — a tiebreaker column keeps the order predictable.
answer: SELECT post_id, user_id, likes FROM posts ORDER BY likes DESC, post_id LIMIT 5;

title: Newest friendships
context: The graph team watches how fresh connections form.
task: Return user_a, user_b and created_at for the five most recently formed friendships.
hint: Sort by when each connection was made, newest at the top, then trim the list.
answer: SELECT user_a, user_b, created_at FROM friendships ORDER BY created_at DESC, friendship_id LIMIT 5;

title: Engagement rate
context: Analysts express engagement as a share of the audience reached.
task: Return post_id and engagement_pct (to 2 decimals): likes, comments and shares combined, as a percentage of reach.
hint: Add the three engagement columns, divide by reach and scale to a percentage — keep the division decimal, not whole-number.
answer: SELECT post_id, ROUND((likes + comments + shares) * 100.0 / reach, 2) AS engagement_pct FROM posts;

title: Ad click-through rate
context: The ads team reports click-through rate per campaign.
task: Return advertiser and ctr_pct (to 2 decimals): clicks as a percentage of impressions.
hint: A ratio of two columns scaled to a percentage — keep the division decimal.
answer: SELECT advertiser, ROUND(clicks * 100.0 / impressions, 2) AS ctr_pct FROM ad_campaigns;

title: Cost per click
context: Finance measures how much each click costs an advertiser.
task: Return advertiser and cpc (to 2 decimals): spend divided by clicks.
hint: Divide spend by clicks — nudge it to decimal so whole-number division doesn't truncate the result.
answer: SELECT advertiser, ROUND(spend * 1.0 / clicks, 2) AS cpc FROM ad_campaigns;

title: Display-name width
context: Design is checking how wide display names get.
task: Return each user's name alongside name_len, the number of characters in it.
hint: There's a function that returns the length of a piece of text.
answer: SELECT name, LENGTH(name) AS name_len FROM users;

title: Build a handle
context: A migration generates an @-handle from each user's name.
task: Return handle for every user: an @ sign followed by the name in lower case.
hint: Force the name to lower case, then stitch an @ in front of it.
answer: SELECT '@' || LOWER(name) AS handle FROM users;

title: Posts per platform
context: A dashboard shows where people are posting.
task: Return each platform and the number of posts published on it.
hint: Collapse the posts to one row per platform, then count within each.
answer: SELECT platform, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY platform;

title: Reaction mix
context: The team wants the overall breakdown of reaction types.
task: Return each reaction type and how many times it occurs (as n), most common first.
hint: One row per reaction type; rank them by how often each appears.
answer: SELECT reaction, COUNT(*) AS n FROM reactions GROUP BY reaction ORDER BY n DESC, reaction;

title: How many people post?
context: Growth wants the count of users who have posted at all, not the post count.
task: Return posters: the number of different users who have published at least one post.
hint: The same user appears on many posts — count each one only once.
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS posters FROM posts;

title: Total reach
context: A headline slide needs the platform's combined reach.
task: Return total_reach: the reach of every post added together.
hint: Add up the reach column across all rows.
answer: SELECT SUM(reach) AS total_reach FROM posts;

title: Ad spend by platform
context: Finance splits advertising revenue across the apps.
task: Return each platform and its total ad spend.
hint: Add up spend within each platform.
answer: SELECT platform, SUM(spend) AS spend FROM ad_campaigns GROUP BY platform;

title: Which format earns likes?
context: The content team compares typical likes across post formats.
task: Return each post_type and its average likes (to 1 decimal).
hint: Take the mean of likes within each format.
answer: SELECT post_type, ROUND(AVG(likes), 1) AS avg_likes FROM posts GROUP BY post_type;

title: Average age by country
context: Demographics wants the typical user age in each market.
task: Return each country and the average age of its users (to 1 decimal).
hint: Average age within each country.
answer: SELECT country, ROUND(AVG(age), 1) AS avg_age FROM users GROUP BY country;

title: Reach extremes
context: Analysts want the span between the smallest and largest post reach.
task: Return min_reach and max_reach across all posts in a single row.
hint: The lowest and the highest, side by side.
answer: SELECT MIN(reach) AS min_reach, MAX(reach) AS max_reach FROM posts;

title: Market sizes
context: A map widget ranks countries by how many users they have.
task: Return each country and its user count, most populous first.
hint: Collapse to one row per country, then rank by how many.
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS users FROM users GROUP BY country ORDER BY users DESC, country;

title: Likes earned per user
context: Creator payouts depend on the likes a user's content earns.
task: Return each posting user's user_id and total_likes, the likes summed across all their posts.
hint: Add up likes within each user.
answer: SELECT user_id, SUM(likes) AS total_likes FROM posts GROUP BY user_id;

title: Most prolific posters
context: The team spotlights the five busiest posters.
task: Return user_id and post count for the five users who have published the most.
hint: Count posts per user, rank the totals, and keep only the top few.
answer: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY posts DESC, user_id LIMIT 5;

title: Power users
context: Community wants users who post heavily, above a set threshold.
task: Return user_id and post count for users who have published more than 8 posts.
hint: The threshold applies to each user's post total — filter on the grouped count, not on individual posts.
answer: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 8;

title: Feed with author names
context: A readable feed export needs each post's author name, not just an id.
task: Return post_id, the author's name (as author) and likes for every post.
hint: The author's name lives on the users table — connect each post to the user who wrote it.
answer: SELECT p.post_id, u.name AS author, p.likes FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.user_id = p.user_id;

title: Posts by Indian creators
context: A regional programme surfaces content from local creators.
task: Return post_id and platform for posts written by creators based in India.
hint: Bring in each post's author, then keep only the ones who are creators from that country.
answer: SELECT p.post_id, p.platform FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.user_id = p.user_id WHERE u.country = 'India' AND u.is_creator = 1;

title: Reach by country
context: Leadership wants to see where content travels the furthest.
task: Return each country and the total reach of posts made by users from it.
hint: Link each post to its author, then total reach within each country.
answer: SELECT u.country, SUM(p.reach) AS reach FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY u.country;

title: Reactions earned per author
context: A creator scorecard counts the reactions a user's posts attract.
task: Return each author's user_id and reactions_received, the number of reactions landing on their posts.
hint: Reactions attach to posts, and posts belong to users — count the reactions, grouped by the post's author.
answer: SELECT p.user_id, COUNT(*) AS reactions_received FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id GROUP BY p.user_id;

title: Age bracket
context: Ad targeting buckets users into standard age bands.
task: Return user_id and a bracket label: '18-24' up to age 24, '25-34' up to 34, '35-44' up to 44, otherwise '45+'.
hint: Assign a label by testing age against the cut-offs in ascending order.
answer: SELECT user_id, CASE WHEN age <= 24 THEN '18-24' WHEN age <= 34 THEN '25-34' WHEN age <= 44 THEN '35-44' ELSE '45+' END AS bracket FROM users;

title: Posting trend by month
context: The content team tracks how posting volume moves month to month.
task: Return month (as YYYY-MM) and the number of posts in each, oldest month first.
hint: Derive a year-and-month from each post's date, then count and sort by it.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', post_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;
